title: Synthetic legacy sample

data.title: StatsBomb Open Data
data.use: Use the README, competition list, match files, event schema, and attribution terms. Select a historical competition with enough matches.

isl.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning · Python
isl.use: Use selected chapters and Python labs. The book PDF is free on the authors’ site.

math.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
math.use: Use selected sections as a reference after the visual experiment. The authors provide a free PDF.

visual.title: 3Blue1Brown · visual mathematics
visual.use: Find the linear algebra and calculus lessons. Recreate one visual idea in code.

d2l.title: Dive into Deep Learning
d2l.use: Use the interactive book for calculus, automatic differentiation, training loops, and attention.

tabpfn.title: Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model · 2025
tabpfn.use: Read the question, evaluation design, and limitations. Reproduce one feasible comparison, not the original training run.

paper2026.title: Why Large Language Models Fail at Tabular Prediction · August 2026
paper2026.use: Treat this preprint as a claim to examine. Compare its evaluation choices with your soccer experiments. No paid API experiment is required.

research.title: Anthropic research
research.use: Select a recent public article about evaluations or model behavior. Follow its paper or methods link and record limitations.

careers.title: Anthropic careers
careers.use: Compare your evidence with a current engineering role. Requirements change. This curriculum does not guarantee a role or a credential.

modules.title: Start with a forecast
modules.question: Can a simple rule predict a match?
modules.outcome: Build a reproducible match table and a baseline: a simple reference prediction.
modules.math: Refresh fractions, ratios, percentages, means, variables, functions, and summation through match statistics.
tasks: Load historical matches. Record the source, download date, license, and a small data dictionary.
Create chronological training, validation, and untouched test sets. Count missing and duplicate rows.
Predict home/draw/away using training-set frequencies. Compute accuracy and Brier score, the squared error of probabilities.
Explain why a post-match statistic leaks the answer into a pre-match forecast. Record your baseline and evidence.
weeks: Week 1: Spend 6 h on data and code, 3 h on algebra through match summaries, and 2 h on a data audit.
Week 2: Spend 6 h on baselines, 3 h on probability arithmetic, and 2 h on evaluation and reflection.
modules.evidence: A runnable baseline, a data dictionary, split dates, and a one-page explanation of what the model knows before kickoff.
modules.challenge: Recompute a three-outcome Brier score for one match. Explain why all three probabilities must sum to one.
modules.reading: ISL chapter 2. Use a small competition first. Preserve the same held-out test period throughout the project.
modules.dataset: StatsBomb Open Data: competitions.json → matches/{competition_id}/{season_id}.json. Use scores, dates, and information available before kickoff. Build recent-form features only from earlier matches.

modules.title: Make the mathematics visible
modules.question: How do numbers become a model?
modules.outcome: Build a small interactive forecast with adjustable weights for recent form and home advantage.
modules.math: Refresh equations, slopes, powers, exponentials, logarithms, function composition, and coordinate plots.
tasks: Plot a weighted score as you vary each input. Label the units and ranges.
Convert scores to three probabilities with softmax, a function that turns scores into normalized probabilities.
Plot squared error and log loss as predictions become confidently wrong. Recreate one calculation without a model library.
Write what each symbol means and translate the formula into a small Python function.
weeks: Week 3: 6 h building the forecast, 3 h on functions and plots, 2 h explaining your outputs.
Week 4: 6 h exploring losses, 3 h on powers and logarithms, 2 h recording counterexamples.
modules.evidence: A notebook with adjustable inputs, labeled plots, and examples of confident errors.
modules.challenge: Explain why a tiny probability for the actual outcome produces a large log loss. Calculate one example.
modules.reading: ISL chapters 2 and 4. Use logarithms as measurements of multiplicative change.
modules.dataset: StatsBomb Open Data: competitions.json → matches/{competition_id}/{season_id}.json. Use scores, dates, and information available before kickoff. Build recent-form features only from earlier matches.

nextPhase: Deeper probability, Bayesian inference, optimization, and proof-based reasoning.
Large-scale training, distributed systems, GPU programming, and performance engineering.
Language-model training and evaluation, interpretability, and a sustained open-source contribution.
A larger research reproduction with mentorship and role-specific interview practice.
